g.title: DILI_QSP
g.text: Drug-Induced Liver Injury (DILI) — QSP Mechanistic Map
Drug-induced liver injury · Quantitative Systems Pharmacology map
Reactive-metabolite flux vs. thiol resynthesis · mitochondrial bioenergetics · JNK–Sab bistable amplification ·
bile-acid (BSEP) cholestasis · innate DAMP signalling · HLA-restricted adaptive immunity · regeneration reserve
Central claim: injury = f(production rate / disposal rate), and the system is bistable — so the same AUC can be silent or fatal.

g.title: ZONAL
g.text: necrosis begins where CYP2E1 is highest

g.title: ADAPT
g.text: — the outcome for most of those exposed

g.title: AUTOPH
g.text: clearance of adducts and damaged organelles

g.title: SEPARAT
g.text: the unstable boundary between adaptation and necrosis
— the real definition of the antidote window

g.title: ALT
g.text: = surrogate for the RATE of cell death

g.title: CYP7A1
g.text: rate-limiting step of bile acid synthesis

g.title: HEPVIABLE->SEPARAT
g.text: reserve shifts the position of the separatrix

g.title: MONITOR
g.text: ALT follow-up on isoniazid and anti-TB therapy

g.title: RUMACK
g.text: (valid only for a single acute ingestion)

g.title: REEXPO
g.text: rapid, severe recurrence — contraindicated in principle

g.title: STOPDRUG
g.text: Immediate withdrawal of the causative drug

g.title: NAC->SEPARAT
g.text: pushes the trajectory back below the separatrix
(window = the time at which the separatrix is reached)

g.title: UDCA
g.text: cholestatic type · hydrophilises the bile acid pool

g.title: MARS
g.text: high-volume plasma exchange improves ALF survival

g.title: DEPRESCR
g.text: Switch to an alternative agent · no rechallenge
